decision_reason: A1 leaves the low-U_NN pair standing still and sitting and relaxing separated only by a broad posture-inclination coordinate, while walking differs from its closest seen anchor jogging only in motion intensity. The weakly covered jump front & back also needs a distinction between alternating translation and sustained locomotor progression. A2 therefore decomposes posture and translation, adds periodic impact loading and translation-direction reversal, and removes motion_regularity because every supplied class prototype has the same level.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: trunk_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the chest or trunk within a window, independent of the orientation of the distal limbs.

levels.Low: Trunk is nearly upright relative to gravity.
levels.Medium: Trunk is moderately inclined relative to gravity.
levels.High: Trunk is strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: segment_orientation_misalignment
attributes.definition: Degree of gravity-relative orientation difference between the trunk and distal lower limb, indicating an articulated rather than uniformly aligned body configuration.

levels.Low: Trunk and distal lower limb have similar or nearly aligned gravity-relative orientations.
levels.Medium: Trunk and distal lower limb have a moderate orientation difference.
levels.High: Trunk and distal lower limb have a pronounced orientation difference.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: locomotor_progression
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained translational progression through space within a window, excluding translation that is mainly oscillatory or repeatedly reversed.

attributes.name: vertical_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of translation or oscillation along the gravity-relative vertical direction during the activity.

attributes.name: periodic_impact_loading
attributes.definition: Degree to which repeated motion cycles contain recurring foot-strike or landing-like abrupt loading events, independent of their repetition rate.

levels.Low: Repeated impact loading is absent or weak.
levels.Medium: Motion cycles contain recurring moderate impacts.
levels.High: Motion cycles contain recurring pronounced impacts.

attributes.name: translation_direction_reversal
attributes.definition: Degree to which translational motion repeatedly reverses direction within a window rather than maintaining one progression direction.

levels.Low: Little translation or little directional reversal.
levels.Medium: Occasional or partial reversal of translational direction.
levels.High: Clear and repeated alternation of translational direction.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains a direct supported distinction between weakly moving postures, walking, and vigorous locomotor or jumping activities.
Repetition rate is physically distinct from impact magnitude and remains transferable from periodic seen locomotor activities.
Sustained rapid fluctuation separates continuous relaxed or cyclic motion from abrupt jumping and running patterns and is independently supported by rapid-change behavior.
Peak-like impacts are physically distinct from sustained roughness and provide a transferable link between jump front & back and impact-rich seen locomotion.

The broad global inclination concept conflates whole-trunk tilt with articulated posture. Chest and ankle orientation permit these concepts to be separated, adding a supported configuration contrast for standing still versus sitting and relaxing while retaining lying down as a recumbent seen anchor.
Time-varying global posture is distinct from mean trunk orientation and helps separate static postures from jumping or repeated whole-body flexion.
Angular-motion prominence remains directly observable and distinguishes static postures from locomotor and articulated cyclic movement without duplicating linear progression.

General translation conflates sustained progression with gravity-axis displacement. Separating them distinguishes walking from climbing stairs and identifies the strong vertical component of jump front & back without treating its alternating front-back motion as continuous progression.
Every supplied A1 prototype has High motion_regularity, so the concept provides no split-specific class contrast and would consume capacity without improving unseen separation or seen support.

Recurring loading events provide a second physically supported contrast between walking and its nearest seen anchor jogging beyond overall intensity. The attribute also transfers through running to the repeated landing structure of jump front & back while remaining distinct from cadence and isolated peak impulsiveness.

Repeated front-back reversal is the defining transferable distinction of jump front & back from sustained locomotion. Short-window translational proxies and multiaxial motion structure can support this contrast without assuming net displacement.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final attributes describe distinct physical factors. Motion_intensity measures total energy; cadence measures repetition rate; smoothness measures sustained rapid fluctuation; impulsiveness measures isolated peak changes; and periodic_impact_loading measures whether impacts recur across cycles. Trunk_inclination captures mean chest posture, segment_orientation_misalignment captures articulated trunk-to-lower-limb geometry, and posture_variability captures temporal change in global posture. Rotational_motion is angular, whereas locomotor_progression, vertical_translation, and translation_direction_reversal respectively describe sustained linear advancement, gravity-axis translation, and alternation of translation direction. Although some activities may express several factors together, none of these attributes is defined as a restatement of another.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
